2013|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/ricardo-ledo|access-date=June 12, 2013}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Trotamundos de Carabobo]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (SPB). He committed to play for the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]], but the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) ruled him academically ineligible to play during his freshman season in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]].{{cite web| last =Lombardi| first =Matt| title =Providence's Best Recruit In Years, Ricky Ledo, Declares For The NBA Without Even Playing A Game For The Friars| work=CollegeSpun.com |publisher =College Spun, LLC.| date =April 11, 2013| url =http://collegespun.com/big-east/providence/providences-best-recruit-in-years-ricky-ledo-declares-for-the-nba-without-even-playing-a-game-for-the-friars#| access-date =June 13, 2013}} Ledo never played for the Friars that season, and at the end of the year he declared he was entering the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{cite web| title =Ricky Ledo didn't play a game at Providence last year, still among top point guards in draft| work=FoxNews.com | publisher = FOX News Network, LLC.| date =June 4, 2013| url =https://www.foxnews.com/sports/ricky-ledo-didnt-play-a-game-at-providence-last-year-still-among-top-point-guards-in-draft/| access-date = June 10, 2013}} ==High school career== During his high school career, Ledo spent his first two years enrolled at Bishop Hendricken High School in Warwick, Rhode Island. Ledo attended [[St. Andrew's School (Rhode Island)|St. Andrew's School]] in [[Barrington, Rhode Island]], [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)|Notre Dame Preparatory School]] in [[Fitchburg, Massachusetts]], and [[South Kent School]] in [[South Kent, Connecticut]].{{cite web| last =Farrahar| first =Kevin| title =Breaking Down Ricky Ledo| work =FriarBasketball.com| publisher =Wordpress| date =June 2, 2013| url =http://friarbasketball.com/2013/06/breaking-down-ricky-ledo/| access-date = June 13, 2013}} At St. Andrew's, Ledo's squad finished second in the NEPSAC Class B conference; at Notre Dame, he led the team to the Prep National Finals; and, at South Kent, he was a Second Team All-Conference performer as a senior. ==College ineligibility== Ledo was rated the #21 overall college prospect by [[ESPN]] and was a McDonald's All-American.{{cite web| title =NBA Draft 2013: Ricky Ledo scouting report| work =SB Nation NBA News| publisher =[[Vox Media, Inc.]]| date =May 1, 2013| url =https://www.sbnation.com/2013/6/9/4403280/ricky-ledo-scouting-report-nba-draft-2013 |access-date =June 13, 2013}} He committed to play for [[Providence College]] in his home state of Rhode Island. In September of his freshman year, the NCAA ruled him academically ineligible due to not having enough credits. He stayed at school with the hope that he would be eligible during the second semester, but the NCAA never reinstated him. ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2013–2015)=== After spending one year at Providence without being able to play, Ledo declared for the [[2013 NBA draft]]. Despite never playing a single game in his career with Providence, he is still credited by the NBA as a player who came out of Providence as opposed to high school. Ledo was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 43rd overall pick in the 2013 NBA draft. His draft rights were then traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and finally to the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On July 24, 2013, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Mavericks.{{cite web| last=MacMahon | first=Tim | title=Mavs sign second-round pick Ricky Ledo | work=ESPN.com | publisher =ESPN, Inc. | date=July 24, 2013 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4697279/mavs-sign-second-round-pick-ledo | access-date=July 25, 2013}} During his rookie and sophomore seasons, he had multiple assignments with the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 8, 2015}} In order to make room for the signing of [[Amar'e Stoudemire]], the Mavericks waived Ledo on February 18, 2015, after appearing in just 16 games over two seasons.{{cite web|first=Brad|last=Townsend|url=http://mavsblog.dallasnews.com/2015/02/mavericks-make-amare-stoudemire-signing-official.html/|title=Mavericks officially sign Amar'e 2015}} On March 3, he re-joined the Texas Legends.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4933364|title=Legends Acquire Ricky Ledo|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 3, [[Turkish Basketball Super League|BSL]] games and twelve [[EuroLeague]] games. In January 2018, he was acquired by the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{cite news|title=Ricky Ledo to join Wisconsin Herd|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/usa/g-league/262690/ricky-ledo-to-join-wisconsin-herd.html|access-date=January 26, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=January 26, 2018}} where he played in 17 games, averaging 15.3 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.6 steals in 33.9 minutes.{{cite news|title=Ricky Ledo player profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Ricky-Ledo/Summary/24251|access-date=January 26, 2018|work=RealGM.com}} On March 27, after the G League season concluded, he signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of the Puerto Rican League.{{cite news|title=Ricky Ledo signs with Vaqueros de Bayamon|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/america/puerto-rico/269424/ricky-ledo-signs-with-vaqueros-de-bayamon.html|access-date=April 15, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=March 27, 2018}} On July 26, 2018, Ledo signed a one-year deal with Italian club [[Pallacanestro Reggiana]].{{cite news|title=Pallacanestro Reggiana signs Ricky Ledo |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/283455/pallacanestro-reggiana-signs-ricky-ledo.html|access-date=July 27, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|date=July 26, 2018}} On November 29, 2018, Pallacanestro Reggiana announced that they have parted ways with Ledo.
